questions.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)$ given that its derivative ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$ are as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\sqrt{3}\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,k,\,{T}^{′}(t)=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{2}\,i-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{2}\,k\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{2})}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{(\frac{-\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{4}({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\frac{1}{2} \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(\sqrt{3})^{2}+(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)+3} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the curvature is 

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{(\frac{1}{2})}{2}=\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s,$ where

$$
r(s)=⟨\frac{1}{3}(1-2s)^{3/2},\,\frac{1}{3}(2s)^{3/2}⟩,\,0<s<\frac{1}{2}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{1}{3}(1-2s)^{3/2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{1}{3}(2s)^{3/2})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{3}{2}\cdot (1-2s)^{1/2}\cdot (-2),\,\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{3}{2}\cdot (2s)^{1/2}\cdot 2⟩ \\  & =⟨-(1-2s)^{1/2},\,(2s)^{1/2}⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-(1-2s)^{1/2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}((2s)^{1/2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{2}\cdot (1-2s)^{-1/2}\cdot (-2),\,\frac{1}{2}(2s)^{-1/2}\cdot 2⟩ \\  & =⟨(1-2s)^{-1/2},\,(2s)^{-1/2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

  

Finally, the curvature is  

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{((1-2s)^{-1/2})}^{2}+{((2s)^{-1/2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(1-2s)^{-1}+(2s)^{-1}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{1-2s}+\frac{1}{2s}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2s(1-2s)}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)$ given that its derivative ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)={e}^{t}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,{T}^{′}(t)=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t),$ we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${T}^{′}(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =|-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}|\sqrt{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\sqrt{({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)+({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)+(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\sqrt{1+1+0} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \sqrt{2} \\  & =1 \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & ={e}^{t}\sqrt{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & ={e}^{t}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t} \\  & ={e}^{t}\sqrt{({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)+({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)+(-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)} \\  & ={e}^{t}\sqrt{1+1+0} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\,{e}^{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\,{e}^{t}}=\frac{\sqrt{2}\,{e}^{-t}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where:

$$
r(s)=⟨\frac{3s+1}{5},\,\frac{3-4s}{5}⟩,\,s\ge 0
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{3s+1}{5}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{3-4s}{5})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{5},\,-\frac{4}{5}⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{3}{5}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\frac{4}{5})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{(0)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$
r(s)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡s,\,1,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡s⟩,\,0\le s<2\pi .
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡s)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡s,\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡s⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡s)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡s,\,0,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡s⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡s)}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{(-\operatorname{cos}⁡s)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡s+{cos}^{2}⁡s} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
